Technology stocks were firming Friday.
Among technology stocks expected to mover on news:
- Domo Inc ( DOMO ) is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select market on Friday after late Thursday pricing a $193 million initial public offering of 9.2 million shares at $21 apiece, near the top of its expected $19 to $22 per share range. The data analytics company also issued a 30-day option to underwriters to buy up to 1.38 million additonal shares to cover overallotments. After paying underwriter discounts and other offering expenses, Domo is expecting to receive around $174.7 million in net proceeds, rising to $201 million if the underwriters fully exercise their overallotment option and is planning to use the new capital for general corporate purposes, including investing in developing new technology to support its growth.
In other sector news:
- Rambus ( RMBS ) fell about 1% in Thursday's late session after the semiconductor components company said it has fired CEO Ron Black, effective immediately, and named general manager Luc Seraphin to take his place on an interim basis. In a statement, the company said the termination follows an incident unrelated to its financial and business performance although his conduct nevertheless fell short of the company standards. The Rambus board has started a formal search process to identify a successor.
- Science Applications International ( SAIC ) late Thursday said it has received a new Pentagon contract with a potential value of up to $116.2 million for providing sustainment support of integrated afloat and ashore tactical networks for the U.S. Department of Defense. The three-year contract also includes one two-year option period which, if exercised, could lift the overall value of the contract to around $196.5 million.
